title: objectql: the lifecycle sweep runs 60 s after every kernel boot, even on a database created seconds earlier, so a fresh tenant kernel pays 130 statements in its first minute
body:
repo:cloud#2 · os-zhuang · session_01QUs3BtyTpTkZhBZdWY1Xun
Ruled: 6663872259 · letter B (item 1) · 2026-11-05T16:47Z

Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named locus and a measured reach. Left over from cloud#3413 after objectstack#28383 (PR #28403) landed; this is item 5 of #28383, which #28403 put out of scope.

## 维护者速读

一个全新环境第一次打开，内核启动 60 秒后就会跑一遍 objectql 生命周期清扫（保留期读取、表计数和悬空引用审计），在 cloud 的托管内核上是 130 条语句。可这时数据库才建好一分钟，没有任何东西需要清理。cloud 的免费环境每次访问只驻留 30 分钟，清扫间隔却是一小时，所以每次访问都付一遍首轮清扫。它现在是空闲内核第一分钟 160 条里的 130 条，cloud#3413 的目标是第一分钟不超过 10 条。

## Reach (measured)

Measured on cloud's hosted tenant composition (`ArtifactKernelFactory` with `HOSTED_FORCED_REQUIRES`, production `TursoDriver` in remote mode over a local libSQL file, every statement counted at the client), framework pin `118bee4d`, with `scripts/dev-local/bootstrap-curve.mjs --hosted --objects 0 --first-boot --hold 1800 --hold-slice 60 --hold-shapes` in objectstack-ai/cloud:

| Run | First minute | What |
|---|---|---|
| default | **160** | 130 in the 50–60 s slice (this card), 20 delivery-dispatcher ramp, 10 `DbQueueAdapter` ramp |
| `OS_LIFECYCLE_DISABLED=1`, same flags, `--hold 120` | **30** | the two ramps only |

A 10-second slicing (`--hold 120 --hold-slice 10`) puts all 130 in one burst at the sweep's initial delay (`DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_INITIAL_DELAY_MS`, 60 s). By shape: 17 retention reads (`SELECT * FROM sys_… WHERE … < ?`), 16 `SELECT COUNT(*)`, the read-only dangling-reference audit over every system table with lookups, and a handful of settings reads on the same clock. At pin `99a6a781` (2026-10-31) the same burst was 94; it grows with the system objects the audit walks.

The sweep interval is an hour (`DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_SWEEP_MS`); cloud evicts a free kernel after 30 idle minutes (`OS_KERNEL_FREE_IDLE_MS`), so a hosted kernel only ever runs the first sweep, and runs it on every boot. On a 2,000-organization launch day with each environment opened once, that is 0.26 million statements of the 0.61 million an idle visit now costs in all.

## Expected

A sweep runs when the data can need one, not once per process start:

1. **Persist a last-swept watermark** (one row, or a `sys_` setting) and, at the initial delay, read it and sweep only when `now − watermark ≥ sweepIntervalMs`. A rebuilt or re-booted kernel then pays one read, not 130.
2. **Seed the watermark when the tables are created.** A database whose system tables were created by this boot has no row older than any retention window, so the first sweep is due one interval later. Without this step item 1 alone does not help the first boot, which is the case measured here.

Cloud could instead push `initialDelayMs` past the 30-minute residency, but then a tenant that visits briefly and often would never be swept, so the fix belongs here.

## Done when

The same reading at the new pin shows no lifecycle-sweep statements in a fresh kernel's first minute (at most the watermark read), a kernel whose watermark is older than the interval still sweeps, and the lifecycle tests still pass. cloud then re-measures under cloud#3413.

## Business reason

- Who benefits: every hosted environment's database reads (Turso quota and bill) and runtime CPU on launch day; self-hosted deployments that restart often the same.
- If not done: the first minute of every visit stays above 100 statements whatever the dispatchers cost, and cloud#3413's target (at most about 10 a minute) cannot be met.

## Reader who acts

objectstack triage routes it to the lane owning `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/` (`lifecycle-service.ts`, and the audit in `integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts` that rides its clock).

## Dedup

Searched objectstack issues, open and closed: "lifecycle sweep initial delay" (6 hits) and "lifecycle sweep watermark" (7 hits). The only relevant one is #28383 (closed), whose item 5 named this and whose PR #28403 left it out of scope. The sibling dispatcher-ramp card is filed alongside this one.
